title: A career shaped by curiosity
sub: Six years of building software, from first principles to production systems.
paragraphs: I’m a Full-Stack Software Engineer with over 6 years of hands-on experience building and shipping production systems across multiple domains, including fintech, HR-tech, and marketplace platforms. I’ve worked across early-stage startups, growing organizations, and large enterprises, building everything from backend architecture and distributed systems to complex frontend applications and real-time interfaces.

My technical background has grown alongside my experience. I started with React and Node.js and gradually moved deeper into the systems behind the application, working across frontend and backend development, databases, cloud infrastructure, distributed services, and real-time systems. I work comfortably across a broad range of technologies, with more emphasis on understanding the system and choosing the right tools than being tied to a particular stack.

I started learning software development while I was still in school and began working independently during high school. Most of my early learning came directly from building things, working with clients, and solving problems I hadn’t encountered before. That grew into professional work across different products and organizations, including freelance development for clients in 20+ countries, followed by work within increasingly larger engineering teams.

As the problems became more complex, my role grew with them. I moved from building applications independently to working on large-scale backend services, production infrastructure, and systems with demanding performance and reliability requirements, eventually taking on technical leadership as a Founding Engineer & Technical Lead. My work has continued to span different kinds of systems while maintaining a broad view of both the product and the engineering underneath it.

Curiosity remains a major part of how I build. I’m interested in what happens beneath the layers of abstraction, not just whether something works from the outside. That means understanding the foundations behind the tools I use, investigating what is actually happening when a system behaves unexpectedly, and learning how different pieces interact rather than treating them as black boxes. I value foundational understanding over simply making things work, because knowing why a system works makes it much easier to reason about, improve, and build on.
